homeTitle: Learn the Dhamma with Win Metta
homeIntro: Win Metta is a nonprofit community that preserves and shares Theravāda Buddhist teachings in Burmese and English. This site is a free place to find Dhamma books and study resources. No account is needed.
homeLibraryText: Search and browse thousands of Dhamma books and study materials in PDF, most of them in Burmese.

aboutIntro: Win Metta is a USA-based California 501(c)(3) nonprofit that preserves and shares Theravāda Buddhist teachings in Burmese and English. We serve learners in Myanmar and around the world.
aboutWork1: Dhamma teaching and meditation instruction in Burmese and English, including guided retreats.
aboutWork2: Pāḷi scripture and Burmese language classes, so more people can read the classical texts.
aboutWork3: Technology and administrative support for monastic communities.
aboutTeachers: Our classes and teachings come from Sayadaws and Venerable monks based in California, Arizona, Myanmar and elsewhere. We share their teachings as given and do not rewrite them.
aboutFree: The Dhamma Library and our teaching materials are free to use, without an account or payment.
aboutMore: More about Win Metta on winmetta.org
privacyIntro: This page explains what this site does with your information. It describes how the site works today.
privacyNone: This site has no accounts, no advertising and no tracking cookies, and it does not use analytics that identify you. It only counts visits anonymously (see "Anonymous visit counts" below). Searching and filtering happen in your browser, and typing a search does not send it to us. See "Search words in the page address" below for one exception.
privacyAnalytics: We count visits so that we can see which pages, classes, retreats, library folders, books and Dhamma posts are used, and in which languages. We use Umami, software that we run ourselves on our own server (hosted with Amazon Web Services in the United States), so no analytics company receives this data. The counting uses no cookies and stores nothing on your device. It does not collect your name, e-mail address, the words you search for, or anything you type. Your IP address is not stored. It is only used to make a hash (a scrambled code that cannot be turned back into the address) that changes every day, so we can count a visitor once a day but cannot recognise the same person on another day. Like any website, we can see the country, region and city (looked up from your IP address, which we do not store), browser, operating system, device type, browser language and time of day that come with each visit, and the website that linked you here (only its address, not the page), but only as totals. We keep the counts for at most 13 months. If your browser sends Do Not Track, we do not count your visit.
privacyStored: If you choose a language, or the languages you read Dhamma posts in, your browser remembers that choice on your device (opening a shared post link that names its languages also sets it) so the site can offer it next time. It is not sent anywhere. If your browser blocks this storage, the site works the same and you can still change language.
privacyHosting: This site's pages and PDF files are delivered by hosting and content delivery providers (currently Amazon Web Services CloudFront for pages and bunny.net for PDF files) and, for the anonymous visit counts above, by our own analytics server at stats.app.winmetta.org, hosted with Amazon Web Services. Like any web service, they process technical information such as your IP address and which pages and files you request, in order to deliver them and keep them secure. We do not use this information to identify or profile visitors.
privacyLinks: Some links lead to other websites, such as winmetta.org. Their privacy practices are their own.

retreatsIntro: Win Metta holds meditation retreats of 3, 7 or 10 days, online on Zoom and in monasteries. Each retreat is led by a Sayadaw or Venerable, with several meditation sessions a day.

retreatsNoneText: New retreats are announced on winmetta.org and on our Facebook page. Past retreats are below.
retreatsHowOnline: Online retreats run on Zoom. The Sayadaw leads several meditation sessions each day. Win Metta volunteers host the Zoom meeting, and in breakout rooms yogis can ask the Sayadaw individual questions about their practice.
retreatsHowOnsite: In-person retreats are held in a monastery. The Sayadaw leads the meditation sessions, and Win Metta volunteers take care of the logistics. Yogis who cannot travel can often join over Zoom.

privacySearchUrlTitle: Search words in the page address
privacySearchUrl: While you search or filter, the site adds your search words, filters and chosen time zone to the page address (for example ?q=…) so that you can bookmark or share the page and use the Back button. The address stays in your browser as you type. But when you open, reload or share such a link, the address is requested from the hosting provider like any other page address, so your search words can appear in its request logs. Please do not put personal information in a search, and share a link only if you are comfortable with its words being visible.

privacyFeedback: When you send feedback, your message, the page and item you report, its language and your interface language are emailed to the Win Metta team through Amazon SNS. Your email address is optional and used only to answer you. Please leave out personal details. Reports are not saved in an application database or request logs; they remain in the recipients’ mailboxes. Opening the form and submitting it send anonymous counts of the context, problem type and success, never the message or email address. The Sādhu button, when available, counts anonymous appreciation clicks. No cookie or storage key is added for either feature. Do Not Track disables these anonymous counts.
